title: Add resumable SSE handshake and fragment-lease to avoid duplicated/partial JSON on resume
author: Maya Patel
release_notes: Improves SSE resume reliability: adds resumable handshake, fragment lease to prevent duplicate partial JSON, and OpenAI-compat adapter hardening. No API surface breaking changes.
description: Context: Customers saw duplicated or truncated JSON objects after reconnect/resume sequences when clients retried SSE connections during transient network errors. Root causes observed in production: (1) race between emitter replay and consumer-offset checkpoint leading to duplicate fragments, (2) ambiguous sentinel/delimiter semantics when fragments split mid-json, and (3) resumption that did not reestablish a strict ordering contract for function/tool-call handoffs. Motivation: Reduce incidence of partial JSON and duplicate events on resume without requiring client changes. Approach summary: introduce a resumable SSE handshake and a short-lived fragment-lease token that the server issues per stream epoch. The handshake binds a resume_token (HMAC-protected, opaque to clients) + fragment_lease_id + initial_offset. On reconnect the client presents the resume_token; the server validates it and either (a) replays fragments from the canonical offset if the lease is still held, or (b) returns a deterministic resync marker instructing client to request a fresh stream slice. Key changes in this PR: 1) Protocol: adds optional headers: X-Redwood-Resume-Token, X-Redwood-Resume-Offset and emits X-Redwood-Fragment-Lease in the initial stream preamble. The resume token is HMACed server-side to avoid leaking internal offsets. 2) Fragment lease: server assigns a per-epoch lease id with a TTL (default 30s). Lease state is stored in ephemeral checkpoint cache (memory + persisted index) to ensure quick validation during resume; expired leases cause a controlled resync. 3) Deterministic sentinel ordering: we normalize stream terminators and function-call sentinels by inserting a lightweight ordinal (seq) on emit that is preserved across resumes. That prevents reorder/double-emit when partial fragments are retransmitted. 4) Escape-normalizer: the stream emitter rewrites split-escape sequences at boundaries to avoid producing invalid JSON when a backslash or multibyte UTF-8 sequence is fragmented. 5) Structured-output fencing: when structured envelopes are used (schema/format hints), the emitter includes a schema_fence marker to ensure resumed fragments belong to the same envelope. 6) OpenAI-compat adapter: compatibility layer accepts the new resume headers and maps them to OpenAI-style reconnect semantics; preserves old behavior when headers absent (backwards compatible). 7) Observability: new metrics (sse.resume.attempts, sse.resume.success, sse.fragment.lease_misses, sse.fragment.lease_replays) and a dedicated dashboard and alert on lease_miss rate. 8) Tests: deterministic unit tests for escape rewriter, integration tests simulating reconnects with mid-json splits, and an e2e canary that runs in perf-lab with synthetic jitter. Commits (high-level): - Initial resumable-handshake protocol surface + HMAC resume token implementation - Add fragment lease lifecycle, TTL config and checkpoint cache integration - Implement ordinal seq tagging and ordered-emit enforcer - Escape normalizer for split-backslash and UTF-8 boundary preservation - OpenAI-compat adapter changes and backwards compatibility tests - Metrics, dashboards, and canary job for perf-lab - Test fixes, flakiness mitigations and documentation in the streaming API changelog Changed areas (high level): - sse/handler.go (handshake headers parsing, token validation) - sse/emitter/* (fragment lease lifecycle, ordinal tagging, escape normalizer) - adapters/openai/compat.go (accept/resume mapping) - observability/metrics_registry.go (new counters/gauges) - tests/sse_resume_integration_test.go, tests/escape_normalizer_test.go - docs/api/streaming.md (document resume headers, migration guidance) Review conversation summary: - Elliot Chen: requested that resume tokens be HMAC-only and that offset not be relied on by clients; asked for TTL config and safety on clock skew. Response: implemented HMAC-only token, added TTL config with default 30s and max 5m guard, added clock-skew tolerance in validation. - Priya Rao: raised concerns around increased memory pressure from storing leases for long-running streams. Response: added eviction policy and persisted minimal index to allow quick rebuild without holding entire payloads; documented tradeoffs. - Jonas Muller: asked for more end-to-end tests covering function-call handoff ordering. Response: added integration cases where function/tool calls are emitted mid-fragment and verified ordinal preserved across reconnects. - QA (internal): reported transient CI flakiness for integration tests due to race in canary setup; fixed by adding deterministic delays and improved test harness teardown logic. CI summary: - Unit tests: pass - Integration tests: pass (after test-fix patch) - Lint/format: pass - Canary job (perf-lab): green on canary nodes, 1% increased latency in worst-case due to preamble exchange but median unchanged. Rollout plan: - Canary 5% of incoming streams in staging for 48h - Observe lease_miss and resume_success metrics, run automated regression eval on a curated prompt set - Gradually increase to 25% then 100% if metrics stable - Feature gate enabled by default for new clusters; cluster-admins can adjust fragment_lease_ttl and resume_hmac_key via config Migration notes for customers: - No client changes required; serverside-only opt-in will be enabled via feature flag during canary. - Advanced clients may supply X-Redwood-Resume-Token/X-Redwood-Resume-Offset to opt into faster resumption (still supported but token is authoritative). - If customers run a custom OpenAI-compat adapter, they should update to accept the new optional headers to benefit from faster resume paths. Merge outcome and follow-ups: - Merged via squash-and-merge. - Follow-up tasks created: ENG-4221 (support longer-lived leases for batch-analytics streams), ENG-4222 (add resume token rotation tooling), SUP-2033 (customer-facing doc and migration notes). Security/privacy notes: resume_token is HMAC with server secret, contains no PII; recommended key rotation process included in ENG-4222. Performance note: small median latency increase on connection startup due to preamble exchange; amortized by fewer duplicate replays and improved success rates.

review_comments: Elliot Chen: please ensure resume token is HMAC-only and not an authoritative offset. Added HMAC-only token and TTL config with clock skew tolerance.
Priya Rao: storing leases could increase memory pressure for many concurrent streams. Added eviction policy and persisted minimal lease index.
Jonas Muller: verify function-call ordering across resumes. Added integration tests asserting ordinals preserved and handoff deterministic.
QA: intermittent canary test failure traced to harness teardown race. Fixed test harness and added deterministic delays in tests.
